text.p: Zannex Securities Ltd on Thursday downgraded Israel's Koor Industries Ltd to a long-term buy from a buy.
"Koor, as the largest conglomerate in Israel, was hit by the Israeli economy slowdown during the fourth quarter (1996)," analyst Tal Liani wrote in a report.
Zannex said the company's building materials division suffered and its telecommunications arm recorded slower sales than expected due to declining sales to Bezeq Israel Telecom.
The telecommunications division was expected to be shadowed by the reduction in sales into 1997, with Zannex expecting a relatively weak first half of the year.
Improvement was expected only in the second half or in 1998 when Zannex also forecast recovery of the construction industry.
"Therefore, based on our expectations for recovery in 1998, mainly in the telecommunications division, we downgrade our recommendation to a long-term buy from buy," Liani said.
Last week Koor reported an 8.4 percent increase in net profit for 1996 to $180.8 million. Koor said exports accounted for 35 percent of its $3.53 billion in revenues.
